sources.note: PSI-39 search record: Flight Platform is 'International Space Station (ISS)' and Project Type is 'Microgravity Investigation'.

objective.value: Characterize low-temperature ('cool flame') combustion of isolated n-dodecane and n-dodecane/iso-dodecane fuel droplets in microgravity: the effect of helium dilution on cool-flame behavior, the relationship between droplet size, pressure and flame extinction, and soot formation during cool-flame burning.

sources.note: PSI-39 search record 'Objectives' lists five aims: n-dodecane and n-dodecane/iso-dodecane combustion at 0.25-5 atm; helium-dilution effects on cool flames; combustion characteristics; droplet-size/pressure/extinction relationship; soot formation.

PSI-39 'Research Impacts': CFI provides 'critical validation for complex chemical kinetic mechanisms', advances low-temperature combustion understanding, and supports safer spacecraft systems. Framed as basic research, not a prevention/detection/suppression device.

safety_functions.note: Classified as fundamental science: neither the challenge brief nor PSI assigns CFI a prevention, detection or suppression role.

sources.note: PSI-39 'Approach': the MDCA 'facilitates the controlled combustion of fuel droplets'; droplets dispensed and suspended between needles or tethered on fibers.
Challenge brief, 'Hardware': FLEX, FLEX-2 and the Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) each featured burning droplets of liquid fuel in the MDCA.

PSI-39 'Approach' and 'Objectives': fuels observed include n-dodecane, farnesane, and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane. Per-test table (PSI-39.csv) lists C12H26 and n-/iso-dodecane blends at 75/25 and 60/40.

fuel_materials.note: Farnesane is named in the PSI approach/objective text but does not appear in the per-test conditions table. 'iso-dodecane' as a pure fuel is not in the per-test table; only appears in mixtures.

fuel_geometry.value: Isolated single fuel droplets, freely deployed between opposed hypodermic needles or supported on a silicon-carbide fiber tether

sources.note: PSI-39 'Approach': droplets of fuel are dispensed and suspended between hypodermic needles or tethered using silicon-carbide fibers.
Dietrich et al. 2024 (CFI results): large, isolated n-dodecane droplets; tests were both free-floated and fiber-supported.

fuel_geometry.note: Initial droplet diameters were large (several mm per the CFI results paper); PSI states no firm size range.

sources.note: PSI-39 'Experiment Hardware': 'Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) / Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)'.
PSI-39 'Approach': the Combustion Integrated Rack contains the MDCA, which facilitates controlled combustion of fuel droplets.
PSI PSI-39 experimental table PSI-39_Experimental table_CFI.csv; per-test conditions, min and max of the listed columns

o2_percent.note: Range over 87 test rows of PSI-39_Experimental table_CFI.csv, columns: Oxygen. Computed by scripts/psi_table_summary.py (initial conditions only).

pressure_psi.note: PSI-39 per-test table gives Pressure 0.5-5 atm; left unknown here because scripts/psi_apply_conditions.py overwrites conditions from that table. The PSI 'Approach' text says 0.25-0.5 atm, inconsistent with the objectives and per-test table.

airflow.note: No airflow value is stated in the PSI-39 record or its per-test table; the MDCA is a quiescent chamber with no imposed flow reported.

sources.note: PSI-39 search record 'Project Type': Microgravity Investigation; Flight Platform ISS. Cool flames need long microgravity times, obtainable only on the ISS.
PSI-39 'Objectives': analyze the effects of helium dilution on cool-flame behavior. Per-test table columns are Nitrogen and Helium (helium fraction 0-0.59, nitrogen 0.2-0.83).

value: Fuel composition (pure n-dodecane vs n-dodecane/iso-dodecane blends at 75/25 and 60/40)
Droplet support (free-floated vs silicon-carbide fiber tether)

sources.note: PSI-39 per-test conditions table (data/source/psi/tables/PSI-39.csv), 87 rows: Pressure, Oxygen, Nitrogen, Helium, Fiber and Fuel columns vary across tests.
PSI-39 'Approach' describes a single common method throughout: MDCA inside the CIR, droplets ignited by a hot-wire igniter that is then retracted; Project Type is Microgravity.

held_constant.note: Inferred as the conditions common to all tests from the one method described.

value: UV camera (OH* emission and flame size)

sources.note: PSI-39 'Approach': black-and-white camera for droplet size, UV camera for OH* radical emissions and flame size, other high-resolution cameras for monitoring, and narrow-/wide-band radiometers for flame radiation. Raw-data file list includes Radiometer_Readings and Chamber_Readings.

relevance_notes.value: Fundamental low-temperature (cool-flame) droplet-combustion and soot study, listed by PSI as related to FLEX (PSI-69). It supplies droplet extinction-diameter and burning-rate data plus chemical-kinetic validation relevant to spacecraft fire safety, since cool flames can precede hot ignition.

sources.note: PSI-39 search record 'Related Investigations': PSI-69 (FLEX); 'Research Impacts' ties CFI to safer spacecraft systems and low-temperature combustion understanding.
NASA CIR operations page: cool flames occur when hydrocarbons are heated in air; their reaction rate first rises then falls with temperature, and they are a precursor to hot ignition.

value: Understanding ignition/autoignition of practical fuels and fuel additives
Design of clean, high-efficiency HCCI engines
Interpretation of octane and cetane numbers
Validation of detailed chemical-kinetic mechanisms for low-temperature hydrocarbon combustion

sources.note: PSI-39 'Research Impacts/Earth Benefits': cool-flame understanding aids new-fuel selection, HCCI engine design, octane/cetane interpretation for spark-ignition and diesel engines, and computational model development.
